newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends slightly higher on export data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends slightly higher on export data.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended slightly higher, boosted by USDA weekly export sales figures that were above expectations, traders said.
USDA on Thursday pegged weekly export sales at 37,600 tonnes, well above expectations for 15,000 tonnes and 51 percent above the four-week average.
"Export sales were certainly better than expected but a lot of it was medium grain rice," a trader said.
The market also drew strength from talk Colombia bought a cargo of U.S. rice, but U.S. export sources said the purchase was made from Argentina.

Traders said the March contract would be supportive to deferred months as the spot month neared expiry on Wednesday. They said cash rice was trading at $11.80 per cwt while futures closed at $11.71 per cwt and prices would likely converge as Wednesday's expiry approached.
Traders said deliveries posted against the March covered longs through February 12 and there were still several longs that intended to take delivery.
Rice ended one to two cents per cwt higher with May up one at $11.62. Volume was estimated by CBOT at 400 lots, compared with Wednesday's volume of 575 lots.
